ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The coil of a small hand-cranked generator has a total of N turns, and each turn can be simplified as a rectangular coil abcd. The magnetic field between the magnetic poles is regarded as a uniform magnetic field, with direction perpendicular to the central axis OO′ of the coil. The coil rotates uniformly about OO′, as shown in Figure 11. The maximum values of the induced electromotive forces produced by side ab and side cd of the rectangular coil are both e_0. Neglecting the resistance of the coil, what is the effective value of the generator's output voltage?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the rectangular coil is labeled a, b, c, d, and is located among multiple uniform magnetic field lines horizontally to the right. The magnetic field direction is labeled B. The coil rotates about the central axis OO′ shown by the dashed line; the OO′ axis is oblique relative to the plane of the figure, and a rotation direction arrow is also drawn at O at the lower left. Side ab and side cd are the two opposite effective sides in the rectangular coil. Reasoning: The problem states that in each turn of the coil, the maximum values of the induced electromotive forces produced by side ab and side cd are both e_0. From the structure in the figure, it can be known that side ab and side cd belong to the opposite effective sides of the same rectangular coil; when the coil rotates in the uniform magnetic field, judging by the right-hand rule, the directions of the induced electromotive forces contributed by these two sides to the external circuit are the same, so the maximum value of the induced electromotive force of a single-turn coil is e_0+e_0=2e_0. There are a total of N turns of the coil, and the turns are connected in series, therefore the maximum value of the total output electromotive force is 2Ne_0. The output of a generator rotating uniformly is sinusoidal alternating current, and its effective value is equal to the maximum value divided by \sqrt{2}, so the effective value of the output voltage is \frac{2Ne_0}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}Ne_0.
